question: Cerebrolysin: human evidence for stroke, TBI, dementia and cognitive decline; mechanism of action; safety profile; dosing; comparisons to other neurotrophic agents; and practical guidance

compound.name: Cerebrolysin
compound.class: Multimodal neurotrophic / neuroprotective peptidergic preparation (porcine brain-derived low-MW neuropeptide + amino acid mixture)

claims.statement: Cerebrolysin improves early (~day 21–30) neurological deficit after acute ischemic stroke vs placebo (NIHSS-type outcomes) when given as add-on IV 30–50 mL/day × 10–21 days.

supporting.notes: Bornstein 2018 MA 9 RCTs N=1879; MW 0.60 for NIHSS day 21/30; NNT ~7.7
Patel 2025 SR/MA 14 RCTs N=2884; ΔNIHSS MD +1.39 (0.53–2.25); declared no industry funding; RoB2+GRADE

contradicting.notes: CASTA mild baseline severity and floor effects limit assay sensitivity in largest single RCT; overall package still industry-heavy

claims.funding_notes: Bornstein package industry-linked; Patel 2025 independent authorship but synthesizes largely industry-funded trials

claims.statement: Cerebrolysin improves day-90 functional independence (mRS) in unselected AIS populations.

supporting.notes: Bornstein day-90 mRS positive mainly in moderate–severe subset only (N=314), not full unselected ensemble

contradicting.notes: CASTA Heiss 2012: pre-specified day-90 global primary not met overall

claims.funding_notes: Discordance between industry MA secondary analyses and largest RCT primary + independent MA dichotomized mRS. Final label Unknown (bordering Speculative for residual subgroup hypotheses only).

claims.statement: Day-90 functional benefit after AIS concentrates in moderate–severe stroke (higher baseline NIHSS).

supporting.notes: Bornstein ordinal mRS day 90 MW 0.61 in NIHSS>12, N=314 — severity-restricted secondary analysis
CASTA post-hoc NIHSS>12 trends including mortality split; hypothesis-generating only

contradicting.notes: No independent confirmatory mRS-primary RCT in severe-only modern reperfusion era; Patel overall mRS 0–2 NS
CASTA overall primary null remains decisive counterweight to subgroup enrichment claims

claims.funding_notes: FINAL ADJUDICATION (Option A, quality gate): certainty = Speculative. Post-hoc/subset N=314, industry MA, no modern severe-only confirmatory RCT. Early NIHSS remains separately Probable (C1). Do not promote moderate–severe day-90 as Probable.

claims.statement: Cerebrolysin as add-on to reperfusion (r-tPA / mechanical thrombectomy) improves early deficit and day-90 functional outcomes, and may reduce hemorrhagic transformation / sICH.

supporting.notes: CEREHETIS: add-on to r-tPA — reduced sICH/early deficit signals reported; day-90 functional outcome not significantly improved on secondary reports
Staszewski 2025: adjunct after MT (small-core cohort) — improved 90-day functional outcomes in that cohort; modest size
Patel pooled HT RR 0.55 (0.32–0.92) exploratory

contradicting.notes: Day-90 function not clearly improved as reperfusion adjunct in CEREHETIS secondary reporting

claims.funding_notes: Early safety/reperfusion compatibility closer to Probable; day-90 functional superiority as reperfusion adjunct remains Speculative

claims.statement: Cerebrolysin improves multidimensional recovery after moderate–severe TBI vs placebo (CAPTAIN-style IV multi-cycle regimens).

supporting.notes: CAPTAIN II: day-90 multidimensional MW_combined ~0.59; safety ≈ placebo
Vester 2021 prospective MA CAPTAIN series supports day 30/90 multidimensional benefit
Jarosz 2023 SR: heterogeneous TBI designs directionally favorable with quality limits

contradicting.notes: CAPTAIN II single-center; industry-linked investigator/statistician network; ensemble endpoint clinical opacity
CAPTAIN I (Poon): ITT primary miss (P<0.1); PP significant — undercuts package robustness

claims.funding_notes: CAPTAIN I EVER sponsor; CAPTAIN II academic funding claim amid same network; low independence as multi-center confirmation

claims.statement: Cerebrolysin improves short–medium-term global clinical impression and cognition in mild–moderate Alzheimer’s disease with cyclic IV therapy.

supporting.notes: Gauthier 2015 MA: cognition SMD −0.40 at 4 wk; global clinical change OR 3.32 (4 wk) and 4.98 (6 mo); global benefit MW 0.57
Wei 2007 earlier CGI-supportive MA

contradicting.notes: 6-month cognition SMD CI crosses null; older small trials; not disease-modification proof

claims.funding_notes: Gauthier EVER SAB; EVER employee coauthor Doppler; Vester coauthor — industry-embedded AD MA

claims.statement: Cerebrolysin has clinically meaningful benefit supporting routine use in vascular dementia.

supporting.notes: Cochrane: small MMSE/ADAS-cog/global benefits possible (e.g., MMSE WMD ~+1)

contradicting.notes: Cochrane explicit: insufficient evidence for routine recommendation; short FU; industry-funded primaries

claims.funding_notes: Review independence high; included trials often industry-supported. Small short-term effect may be Probable; routine-use claim is Speculative/not recommended.

claims.statement: Cerebrolysin prevents incident cognitive decline or dementia in healthy or at-risk adults.

contradicting.notes: AlzDiscovery Cognitive Vitality: prevention unknown; no robust primary-prevention RCTs

claims.statement: SAE and mortality rates with Cerebrolysin are comparable to placebo in AIS trial meta-analyses.

supporting.notes: Strilciuc 2021 safety MA 12 RCTs N=2202; SAE/mortality NS vs placebo
Patel 2025 SAE RR ~1.08 NS; mortality RR 0.86 NS

contradicting.notes: Cochrane AIS Ziganshina lineage: possible increase in non-fatal SAE in some analyses — unresolved discordance

claims.funding_notes: Strilciuc declared no funding/COI but Cluj/Cerebrolysin research network-adjacent; dual-cite Cochrane

claims.statement: Mechanism is multimodal NTF-mimetic pathway modulation (BDNF/NGF/IGF/VEGF-related narratives), not a single receptor agonist.

supporting.notes: Rejdak & Neglur 2023 narrative review of NTF modulation framing

contradicting.notes: Causal chain from specific peptides to clinical mRS remains Speculative; author Ever honoraria/travel COI

claims.funding_notes: MoA literature partly industry-tied narrative reviews

claims.statement: Evidence-based regimens are pharmaceutical IV 10–50 mL/day (indication-specific continuous courses or dementia cycles), not oral or DIY SQ research-chem protocols.

supporting.notes: EVER product monographs: IV infusion primary; IM low volume; labeled contraindications
Stroke MAs/trials consistently 30–50 mL IV × 10–21 d

claims.funding_notes: Monographs industry primary — use for posology only; efficacy certainty is separate

claims.statement: Cerebrolysin monotherapy is superior or clearly equivalent to donepezil, citicoline, or other neurotrophic agents as first-line for AD or stroke.

supporting.notes: Limited AD head-to-head/combo literature (Alvarez lineage) suggests mono Cerebrolysin may be in same ballpark as donepezil short-term on global scales in selected trials — not superiority Established

contradicting.notes: No US guideline positioning as preferred over SOC; no large head-to-head MA vs citicoline

claims.funding_notes: Comparative superiority Unknown; AChEIs remain oral SOC where approved

claims.statement: Combination Cerebrolysin + donepezil is superior to either alone in mild–moderate AD.

supporting.notes: Combo often numerically best on cognition in limited RCTs; BDNF synergy narratives (Alvarez 2016 lineage); safety acceptable in reports

contradicting.notes: Limited RCTs; not standard US practice; Gauthier package industry-embedded

claims.funding_notes: Probable for limited additive/global signal only — not definitive superiority package

claims.statement: Subcutaneous / research-chem / DIY peptide-style Cerebrolysin use is supported by pharmaceutical trial literature.

contradicting.notes: Label/posology: IV infusion primary; IM only low volume
Pivotal stroke/TBI/AD efficacy trials use pharmaceutical IV product

claims.funding_notes: Unknown efficacy outside IV pharmaceutical product; recommend against DIY SQ (harm reduction Established for procedural risk)

claims.statement: Cerebrolysin is not FDA-approved and is not AHA/ASA standard of care for AIS in the United States.

supporting.notes: AHA/ASA 2019 AIS guidelines do not endorse Cerebrolysin as standard US therapy
Not FDA-approved; registered in many non-US jurisdictions only

claims.funding_notes: Inverted to true regulatory/practice fact (quality-gate fix m5); formerly false-claim form with mismatched Unknown/High

recommendations.statement: Where legally available under specialist supervision, consider Cerebrolysin 30–50 mL IV once daily × 10–21 days starting ASAP (≤72 h) as shared-decision adjunct to full standard AIS care (including reperfusion when eligible) aimed at early neurological recovery (NIHSS). Do not present as proven mortality reduction or day-90 functional independence therapy. Unselected day-90 mRS benefit is Unknown; moderate–severe day-90 enrichment is Speculative (hypothesis-generating subset/post-hoc analyses only) — may inform counseling but must not drive a Probable day-90 protocol claim.
recommendations.inference_note: R1 Probable attaches to early NIHSS adjunct dosing (C1), not to C3. C2 day-90 unselected = Unknown. C3 moderate–severe day-90 = Speculative (Bornstein N=314 subset; CASTA post-hoc). Option A quality-gate alignment.

recommendations.statement: For moderate–severe TBI, CAPTAIN-style regimen (e.g., 50 mL IV daily × ~10 days early, then protocolized lower-dose cycles) may be offered as add-on to neurosurgical/ICU/rehab standard care where product is registered.
recommendations.inference_note: Single-center CAPTAIN II + CAPTAIN I ITT miss + industry network downgrade generalizability; signal present

recommendations.statement: For mild–moderate AD in registered markets, cyclic IV 10–30 mL (evidence densest at 30 mL; e.g., 5 days/week × 4 weeks, 2–4 cycles/year) is a reasonable specialist option for short-term global/cognitive support; maintain AChEI/memantine per local guidelines when indicated.
recommendations.inference_note: Short-term CGI/cognition Probable; disease modification Unknown; not US SOC

recommendations.statement: Recommend against routine Cerebrolysin use for vascular dementia outside individualized specialist shared decision after discussing Cochrane limits (small short-term effects, insufficient for routine recommendation).
recommendations.inference_note: Cochrane high-independence stance preferred over industry VaD trial marketing

recommendations.statement: No recommendation for Cerebrolysin for prevention of cognitive decline, anti-aging, or healthy-person cognitive enhancement — evidence absent (Unknown).
recommendations.inference_note: Unknown certainty → no recommendation (DR rule); not a label contraindication

recommendations.statement: Recommend against DIY subcutaneous, research-chemical, gray-market, or oral 'Cerebrolysin-like' products; use only pharmaceutical IV (or label-allowed low-volume IM) product under medical supervision.
recommendations.inference_note: All pivotal efficacy/safety data are pharmaceutical parenteral; DIY efficacy Unknown; infection/identity risks Established

recommendations.statement: Honor label contraindications: hypersensitivity, epilepsy/major seizure disorders, severe renal impairment; screen porcine-origin allergy/cultural constraints; use sterile infusion technique.
Do not frame Cerebrolysin as FDA-approved or AHA/ASA standard US acute stroke therapy; non-endorsement as universal SOC is evidence-aligned for unselected AIS.
recommendations.inference_note: Guidelines vs literature: material mismatch with industry early-NIHSS narrative does not convert to US class I claim

recommendations.statement: Monitor infusion reactions, seizures, renal status, and indication-specific neurological scales (NIHSS/mRS, GCS/GOSE, ADAS-cog/CGI); continue standard stroke/TBI SAE surveillance given residual Cochrane non-fatal SAE discordance.
recommendations.inference_note: Safety ≈ placebo Probable for death/overall SAE; non-fatal SAE unresolved

recommendations.statement: Prefer oral AChEIs as foundational AD pharmacotherapy where approved; treat Cerebrolysin as optional IV adjunct (combination with donepezil has limited Probable additive signals) — not a universal AChEI replacement. Comparative superiority vs citicoline/other neurotrophics is Unknown.
recommendations.inference_note: Indirect comparisons dominate; no large head-to-head MA vs citicoline

recommendations.statement: Recommend against routine use in unselected mild AIS as universal 'everyone gets it' policy — prioritize proven systems of care; NNT/cost/null CASTA primary undermine mild-stroke routine use.
recommendations.inference_note: Assay sensitivity and recovery floor effects in mild stroke

bro_science_claims.claim: Cerebrolysin reverses aging or restores youth
bro_science_claims.literature_note: No anti-aging RCTs or validated rejuvenation endpoints

bro_science_claims.claim: DIY SQ/IM research-chem self-injection cycles enhance IQ/focus in healthy people
bro_science_claims.literature_note: Trials are pharmaceutical IV for stroke/TBI/dementia; no adequate healthy enhancement RCTs; recommend against unsupervised parenteral use

bro_science_claims.claim: Cerebrolysin equals pure recombinant BDNF/NGF therapy
bro_science_claims.literature_note: NTF-mimetic multimodal mixture, not recombinant single-entity NTF drug product

bro_science_claims.claim: Oral capsules or gray-market analogs are interchangeable with IV Cerebrolysin
bro_science_claims.literature_note: Label and pivotal trials are parenteral; oral bioavailability/efficacy not established as clinical equivalent

bro_science_claims.claim: Cerebrolysin is as good as tPA for stroke
bro_science_claims.literature_note: Not a reperfusion agent; mortality benefit not demonstrated; adjunct only

bro_science_claims.claim: Proven universal TBI neurorecovery standard worldwide
bro_science_claims.literature_note: CAPTAIN positive but single-center dominant and industry-linked; not global guideline SOC

bro_science_claims.claim: Better/safer than donepezil for everyone with dementia
bro_science_claims.literature_note: AChEIs remain oral SOC where approved; Cerebrolysin short-term MA support only; route burden differs

bro_science_claims.claim: 50 mL is proven safer than lower doses because SAE RR falls at high dose
bro_science_claims.literature_note: Strilciuc high-dose SAE reduction exploratory only
